notes: Site: Shopify (nkuku.com). The top-level nav 'New' menu item points its own view-all link to /pages/new-arrivals, which was opened and confirmed to be a marketing/editorial landing page (H1 'NEW SEASON', tagline 'Unique by design', no product grid/count -- EXCLUDED per the brief's Collection-page test) that itself links out to the real listings below. The genuine PLPs live at /collections/*: 'New Arrivals' (the umbrella listing, H1 'New Arrivals', real product grid) plus five genuine site-defined per-category children exposed as siblings in the same 'New' mega-menu/drawer: New Furniture, New Lighting, New Kitchen & Dining, New Home Accessories (handle new-home-decor), New Soft Furnishings. A sixth, New Christmas, was found linked from the site's Christmas nav column (same 'new-<category>' URL pattern) and included as a further genuine child. Modeled as one parent row (New Arrivals, is_group true, own qty 208) + 6 child rows, matching the shared engine's grouping-row shape; child qtys do not sum to the parent's because the per-category 'new' cuts and the umbrella 'New Arrivals' listing are independently curated (overlap/non-overlap both possible), which is expected. Qty verified two ways for every row: rendered on-page 'See N items' badge, and exhaustive /collections/<handle>/products.json?limit=250 pagination to an empty page counting unique product IDs; raw /collections.json products_count was checked but not used (matched exactly for new-arrivals=208 but is otherwise known-inflated project-wide). One discrepancy found: New Christmas's rendered badge says 'See 57 items' but exhaustive product enumeration returns exactly 56 unique product IDs (re-verified twice, page 2 always empty) -- the enumerated 56 was used as the more directly verifiable number; badge vs. listing count drift of this kind is a known Shopify quirk (cached count metafield vs. actual collection membership). Checked footer nav, sitemap, and site search for 'new in'/'just arrived'/'latest' -- no other genuine New Arrivals PLP found.
